headline: A 2021 law gives the Alyce Spotted Bear and Walter Soboleff Commission on Native Children two more years, from three to five, to submit its report.
what_it_does: The commission was created to study federal, state, local, and tribal programs that serve Native children and to suggest federal policy plans for them. This law changes the deadline for the commission's report to the President and Congress from three years to five years. The summary does not describe any other changes.

who_it_affects.how: The commission's study of programs that serve Native children will take longer, so any resulting recommendations will arrive later than originally planned.

who_it_affects.group: Tribal governments and tribal programs that serve Native children
who_it_affects.how: The commission's review covers tribal programs, so their input and reporting timeline are affected by the later deadline.

who_it_affects.group: Federal, state, and local agencies that run children's programs
who_it_affects.how: Agencies whose programs the commission is reviewing will have more time before the final report is delivered.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted September 24, 2021; the official summary does not state a separate effective date.
